118.how_to_build: Attach ~더라 to the relevant predicate using the forms in HTSK; the ending itself carries the speaker's firsthand perspective.
examples: 가방이 무겁더라
From my own experience, I realized that the bag is heavy
이민호는 정말 멋지더라
Minho Lee is very stylish (from what I experienced)
한국말을 배우는 게 힘들더라
I realized that learning Korean is hard
문제는 컴퓨터더라
From my own experience, I realized that the problem is the computer
118.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

119.meaning: ~더니 links a past observation with a later change, result or contrast.
119.when_to_use: Use it when the speaker observed one situation and then saw what happened afterward, especially an unexpected result.
119.how_to_build: Attach ~더니 to the first clause and conjugate the following clause normally; follow the subject and tense restrictions described by HTSK.
examples: 의자 등받이에 허리를 대고 오랜 시간 앉았더니 허리가 아파요
I sat with my back against the backrest for a long time and my back is now sore
장난으로 녀석이라는 말을 자주 쓰기 시작했더니 실수로 동생에게 녀석이라고 불렀어요
I started often calling people 녀석 and then by accident called my sister a 녀석
슬기가 체육시간에 너무 많이 달리더니 다음 수업을 들을 수 없었어요
I personally saw/experienced Seulgi run a lot during P.E. class, so she didn’t attend the next class
슬기가 체육시간에 너무 많이 달려서 다음 수업을 들을 수 없었어요
Seulgi ran a lot during P.E. class, so she didn’t attend the next class
119.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

120.meaning: ~다니 is a quoted or exclaimed form used to react with surprise, disbelief or strong feeling toward information.
120.when_to_use: Use it when the speaker is reacting to what was said or what has happened, often with an emotional tone.
120.how_to_build: Form the relevant quotation before 니: verb, adjective, noun and past forms use the contractions explained in HTSK.
examples: 놀이터에 있는 그네가 망가졌다니 믿을 수 없다
I can’t believe that the swing in the playground broke
우리가 만든 드라마의 시청률이 떨어졌다니 너무 실망스러워요
I’m very disappointed that the ratings for the drama we made dropped
동네 내과에 갔더니 대학 병원 내과에 가라고 하다니 점점 걱정이 되기 시작했다
I went to a local clinic, and they told me to go to a university hospital, so I started to get more worried
너의 부모님이 이혼하신다니 안됐다
It’s too bad that your parents will get a divorce (now that I have heard that your parents will get a divorce, it is too bad)
120.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

121.meaning: ~다 보면 means if one continues doing something or as time passes while doing it, a result may occur.
121.when_to_use: Use it for a result that emerges naturally through repeated or continued experience.
121.how_to_build: Attach the appropriate quoted/plain form + 보면 to the first clause and conjugate the result clause normally.
examples: 네가 그렇게 열심히 일하다 보면 승진하게 될 거야
If you continue to work hard like that, you will likely be promoted
이 길을 계속 따라가다 보면 찾고 있는 시장이 나타날 거예요
If you keep following this road, the market you are looking for will appear
고아원에서 봉사를 하다 보면 감사하는 태도로 살아야겠다는 생각이 들어요
After volunteering repeatedly at an orphanage, I realized that I must live with a thankful attitude
바쁘게 살다 보면 가끔 중요한 일을 잊어버려요
If you continue to live a busy life, sometimes you will forget important things
121.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

122.meaning: ~다 보니 means that after doing something or as a result of continuing, the speaker discovered an often unexpected result.
122.when_to_use: Use it when the result becomes apparent through experience rather than being planned in advance.
122.how_to_build: Attach the relevant verb form before 보니, following the contraction and tense patterns shown by HTSK.
examples: 길거리를 걷다 보니 물방울이 느껴져서 비가 온다는 것을 알았어요
While walking down the road, I felt some water droplets, and knew it was raining
그 사람이랑 얘기하다 보니까 세계 서열 1위의 부자일수도 있다고 생각했어요
While talking to that person, I thought it could be possible that she is one of the richest people in the world
아버지와 논쟁하다 보니 이제부터 아버지 말에 복종해야 한다는 것을 깨달았어요
While arguing with my father, I realized that I should have obeyed him (his words) starting from yesterday
그리스라는 나라를 공부하다보니 로마 제국까지 공부해야 한다는 것을 느꼈어요
While studying about the country of Greece, I felt that I should also study up to the Roman Empire
122.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

123.meaning: ~아/어 보니까 means after trying or experiencing something, I found or realized that.
123.when_to_use: Use it when direct experience leads to a discovery or changed understanding.
123.how_to_build: Attach ~아/어 보니까 to the verb stem with the normal vowel rule; the following clause states what was discovered.
examples: 한번 머리를 염색해 보니까 염색이 생각만큼 간단하지 않다는 걸 알게 됐다
Now that I have tried/attempted to dye my hair, I realize/can assert that doing so is not as simple as one thinks
과학 공부를 해 보니까 많은 과학 서적 내용이 검증이 필요하다는 걸 알게 됐다
Having studied science, I now know that the material in science books require a lot of verification
그 회사가 획기적으로 건물 디자인을 구축해 보니까 사람들이 반응이 더 좋았어요
After that company constructed a groundbreaking design for their building, they realized people’s reactions were better
저자가 다른 작가에 좌우되지 않고 책을 더 잘 쓰기 위해 자신에 더 집중해 보니까 더 진지하게 작품을 쓸 수 있게 됐어요
In order to write his own book well, the writer realized that not allowing himself to be influenced by other works allowed him to write his piece more seriously.

124.meaning: ~ㄹ/을 만하다 means worth doing or sufficiently possible, and 가치가 있다 expresses that something has value.
124.when_to_use: Use it to evaluate whether an action or experience is worth the time, effort or risk.
124.how_to_build: Attach ~ㄹ 만하다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을 만하다 after another consonant; use 가치가 있다 in the noun construction from HTSK.
examples: 외국어를 배울 만한 가치가 있어요
It is worth learning a foreign language
해외에서 한 번이라도 살아볼 만한 가치가 있어요
It is worth trying/attempting living in a foreign country at least once
이 묘지 자리가 이렇게 많은 돈을 낼 만한 가치가 있어요?
Is it worth paying this much money for this cemetery plot?
초승달, 보름달이 왜 생기는지 원리를 배울 만한 가치가 있어요?
Is it worth learning the principle behind why there are half-moons and full-moons?
124.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

125.meaning: ~ㄴ/는다니까 is a contracted quoted form used to insist that the speaker has already said something, often with frustration or emphasis.
125.when_to_use: Use it in a response when repeating information that the listener should already know; HTSK warns that it can sound rude or sassy.
125.how_to_build: Start from the plain quoted form + 고 하니까 and contract it: present verbs, past, future, adjectives, nouns and commands have the separate forms shown by HTSK.
examples: 반이상 정답을 맞추면 합격으로 간주한다니까
I already said that if you get more than half correct then it is considered a pass
이런 빵은 너무 두껍다니까
I told you that this kind of bread is too thick
그 사람은 보면 볼수록 예쁘다니까
I told you that the more you look at that person, the more pretty she is
이게 내 것이라니까!
(Ugh, I already said that) this is mine

126.meaning: ~별 after a noun means by category or for each category, while 별로 is an adverb with a negative meaning such as not particularly.
126.when_to_use: Use them when organizing things by type or saying that something is not especially so.
126.how_to_build: Attach 별 to a noun for categories; use 별로 before a negative predicate, following the source examples.
examples: 우리 회사는 분기별로 세금을 내요
Our company pays tax by the quarter
코치가 선수들을 체중별로 나눴어요
The coach divided the athletes by weight
저는 신분증을 나이별로 다 정리했어요
I organized the ID cards by age
모든 나라가 국가별로 대표를 지명했어요
Each country designated a representative separately

127.meaning: ~씩 distributes something by each or at regular intervals. It combines with quantities and adverbs such as 조금씩 and 가끔씩.
127.when_to_use: Use it for equal distribution, repeated intervals or gradual amounts.
127.how_to_build: Attach 씩 to the noun or number being divided; combine it with the quantity or frequency expression in the order shown by HTSK.
examples: 제가 울다가도 가끔씩 웃음이 나요
Even when I cry I laugh sometimes
가끔씩은 규칙을 어기는 것이 괜찮아요
Sometimes it is okay to break the rules
그는 가끔씩 자기방어로 거짓말을 해요
He lies sometimes to defend himself

It seems that people need to try new things every once and a while

128.meaning: ~아/어 놓다 describes an action completed in advance whose resulting state remains.
128.when_to_use: Use it when something has been done and left that way for later, preparation or continued effect.
128.how_to_build: Attach ~아/어 놓다 with the normal vowel rule; conjugate 놓다 and distinguish the continuing result from simply completing an action.
examples: 밖이 갑자기 어두워지고 저는 겁이 나서 커튼을 닫아 놓았어요
Outside got dark all of a sudden, and I was scared so I closed the curtains

129.meaning: 넘다 means pass or exceed a point, amount or threshold. 넘게 and 넘어서 extend this meaning in clauses.
129.when_to_use: Use it for crossing limits, going over quantities or moving beyond a physical or abstract point.
129.how_to_build: Use the noun or number with 넘다, or attach ~게/~어서 in the constructions HTSK demonstrates; conjugate 넘다 normally.
examples: 우리는 강을 넘어서 한강 공원에서 놀았어요
We crossed the river and then played in the Han River Park
그 언덕 넘어서 계속 가다 보면 온천에 도착해요
If you go over the hill and keep going, you will arrive at the hot-spring
어제가 시험 문제 출제 마감일이라서 다 하고 12시 넘어서 잤어요
Yesterday was the deadline for creating exam questions, so I did them all and slept after 12
외계인을 찾으려면 인간은 엄청난 우주를 넘어서 지구와 비슷한 행성을 찾아야 돼요

130.meaning: Korean uses large-number units based on ten-thousand groups, including 만, 억, 조 and larger units.
130.when_to_use: Use the system for prices, populations, money and other large quantities instead of reading every digit as in English.
130.how_to_build: Group digits in sets of four and attach the Korean unit for each group, using the zero and omitted-unit rules explained on the official lesson page.
examples: 대략 1조 원 이상의 재산이 있는 사람은 한국에 별로 없어요
There are not many people that have more than around a trillion dollars in Korea
“조” 하고 다음 숫자 단위는 “경”이에요
After 조, the next Korean number unit is 경
대략적으로
roughly
우주 나이는 대략 백삼십억 살이에요
The age of the universe is roughly 13,000,000,000 years

131.meaning: 사이시옷 is a spelling and pronunciation feature that can appear between parts of certain compound nouns.
131.when_to_use: Use it when reading or forming the compound nouns covered by Korean orthographic and pronunciation rules.
131.how_to_build: There is no free productive suffix. Learn which compounds take ㅅ and apply the pronunciation and spelling patterns listed by HTSK.
examples: 바람이 너무 세서 촛불이 꺼졌어요

아주 어두워서 반딧불이 잘 보여요

That outcast speaks to himself a lot whenever he eats lunch

In order to save paper, you should always use the back side of the page
131.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

132.meaning: ~ㄹ/을수록 means the more or as something increases, the more another result changes.
132.when_to_use: Use it for proportional or parallel changes in degree, frequency or amount.
132.how_to_build: Attach ~ㄹ수록 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을수록 after another consonant; the result clause states the corresponding change.
examples: 수업 시간이 단축될수록 학생들이 기뻐해요

As it gets closer to the peak season, the price of accommodation gets more expensive
애기가 피곤할수록 애기를 재우기가 더 쉬워요

133.source_title: There is no way with ~ㄹ/을 리가 없다
133.meaning: ~ㄹ/을 리가 없다 means there is no way that something is true or will happen.
133.when_to_use: Use it to strongly deny a possibility or say that an outcome is impossible based on reason or expectation.
133.how_to_build: Use the noun 리 with the modifier ~ㄹ/을 and add 가 없다; apply the consonant-vowel rule before 리.
examples: 뚜껑이 그냥 다 없어질 리가 없어요

원유 값이 작년처럼 떨어질 리가 없어요
There is no way that the price of oil will drop like last year
선생님이 자기 제자를 용서할 리가 없어요

134.meaning: Konglish consists of Korean words borrowed or adapted from English and used with Korean pronunciation and meaning.

sandwich

shopping mall
버튼
button

135.meaning: 성 has several meanings and readings depending on the Hanja-based word in which it appears.
135.when_to_use: Use context and the complete word to distinguish the meanings introduced by HTSK.
135.how_to_build: This is vocabulary rather than one ending; learn 성 compounds and their pronunciation and meanings as listed on the official page.

136.meaning: ~기에 and ~길래 can give a reason, with different perspectives and discourse nuances.
136.when_to_use: Use them when explaining a basis or reason, especially when the speaker's discovery or situation motivates the following statement.
136.how_to_build: Attach ~기에 or ~길래 to the first clause using the forms in HTSK; the second clause gives the consequence or response.
examples: 소고기가 마트에서 할인하길래 많이 사 왔어요
Beef was on sale at the supermarket, so I bought a lot of it
그 여자가 너무 예쁘길래 전화번호를 물어봤어요
That girl was very pretty, so I asked for her number
양반다리를 하고 앉길래 당신의 자세가 불편하다고 생각했어요
You were sitting cross-legged, so I thought you were uncomfortable
저는 배가 고파서 밥을 많이 먹고 싶어요
I am hungry, so I want to eat a lot
136.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

137.meaning: ~아/어야 can express necessity or a condition without the full 하다 expression.
137.when_to_use: Use it in constructions where the required condition or action is followed by a result, command or conclusion.
137.how_to_build: Attach ~아야 after a ㅏ/ㅗ stem and ~어야 after other vowels; 하다 becomes 해야, then add the following clause or predicate.
examples: 사람들은 물을 마셔야 살아요
Only if people drink water will they live
사람들이 물을 안 마시면 죽어요
If people don’t drink water, they die
그래야 맛있어요
Only if you do it like that will it be delicious
그래야 집중을 잘 할 수 있어요
Only if you do it like that can you concentrate well
137.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

138.meaning: ~았/었어야 하다 means should have done or was supposed to have done something in the past.
138.when_to_use: Use it for past obligation, regret or criticism about what ought to have happened.
138.how_to_build: Use the past form before 어야 하다: V-았/었어야 하다, then conjugate 하다 for the sentence ending.
examples: 예방 접종을 맞아야 했어요
I must have gotten a vaccination
달빛이 예뻐서 사진을 찍었어야 해요
The moon (light) was so pretty, I should have taken a picture
몸살이 나기 전에 병원에 갔어야 해요
You should have gone to the hospital before your body started aching
수돗물 말고 애기한테 생수를 먹였어야 해요
You should have given/fed the baby mineral water instead of tap water
138.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

139.source_title: It was okay to with ~았/었어도 되다
139.meaning: ~았/었어도 되다 means it was okay or permitted to do something, even though the action is in the past.
139.when_to_use: Use it to say that a past action would have been acceptable or that permission existed.
139.how_to_build: Attach the past 아/어 form before 어도 되다, then conjugate 되다; use the negative or question patterns from HTSK when needed.
examples: 제비뽑기를 해서 일을 맡기는 것 대신에 그냥 저한테 맡겼어도 돼요
Instead of assigning that job by drawing straws, you could have just assigned it to me
현혈하는 것이 위험한 수술이 아니라서 오기 전에 아무거나 먹었어도 돼요
Giving blood is not a dangerous surgery, so you could have eaten anything before you came
이 야채에 살충제를 안 뿌려서 안 씻어도 돼요
There isn’t/wasn’t pesticides sprayed on these vegetables, so you don’t need to wash them
기름을 넣지 않았어도 됐어요
You didn’t need to put gas in it
139.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

140.meaning: ~(으)로서 means as a role, capacity or position.
140.when_to_use: Use it to identify the role from which someone acts or is evaluated.
140.how_to_build: Attach ~로서 after a vowel and ~으로서 after a consonant; place it after the noun naming the role.
examples: 그 사람은 운동선수로서 한국에서 유명하다
That person is famous as an athlete in Korea
그 사람은 하버드 대학의 졸업생으로서 제일 똑똑한 학생 중 한 명이었다
That person was known as one of the smartest graduates of Harvard University
엄마로서의 삶은 내가 생각한 것보다 훨씬 어려웠다
Life as a mom was much more difficult than I thought
저의 새 언니가 아내로서는 좋지만 엄마로서는 별로예요
My sister-in-law is good as a wife, but not as a mother
140.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

141.meaning: ~(으)로써 means by means of, through or by using something.
141.when_to_use: Use it to name the method, tool or means by which an action is accomplished.
141.how_to_build: Attach ~로써 after a vowel and ~으로써 after a consonant; place it after the noun representing the means.
examples: 이곳은 마당으로써 사용해도 되고 정원으로써 가꿔도 돼요
You can use this place as a yard, or grow a garden
저는 이별의 선물로써 남자친구에게 가장 아끼는 신발을 줬어요
I gave my boyfriend my favorite shoes (the shoes I was saving most) as a goodbye present
이 스피커는 인공지능이 있는 기계로써 사람과 대화가 가능합니다
It is possible for this speaker to talk with humans by using an artificial intelligence machine
주말에 일한 것에 대해 별도 수당으로써 상품권이 지급 될 예정이다
For working on the weekend, a gift certificate will be paid as overtime pay
141.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

142.meaning: ~다니 can show a strong attitude or reaction such as surprise, disbelief or amazement at information.
142.when_to_use: Use it when the speaker reacts emotionally to a quoted fact or situation, with the attitude determined by context and intonation.
142.how_to_build: Form the relevant quoted or plain predicate before 다니 using the verb, adjective, noun and tense patterns explained by HTSK.
examples: 좌절했다니? 그 시험을 한번에 통과하는 사람은 거의 없어
I’m frustrated that I couldn’t pass the test on the first try
민망하다니?
I’m embarrassed because I am with you
다듬고 싶다니? 애기 머리에 솜털밖에 없다
I want to trim the baby’s hair this weekend
단백하다니? 기름이 엄청 많은데
This pizza isn’t greasy, it’s very clean/light
142.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

143.meaning: ~ㄹ/을걸요 gives a speaker's guess, confident prediction or correction, often meaning probably or I doubt that.
143.when_to_use: Use it when responding to another person's assumption, making a prediction or gently refuting what was said.
143.how_to_build: Attach ~ㄹ걸요 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을걸요 after another consonant; use the negative form when appropriate.
examples: 오늘은 추석이라서 식당이 안 열었을걸
Today everybody will probably go to that Korean restaurant
아닐걸. 그렇게 하면 은박지에서 해로운 물질이 나올걸
Cooking meat in tinfoil can’t be bad for one’s health, right?
아닐걸요. 의사선생님은 단순한 찰과상이라고 할걸요
You fell and hurt your knee bad, do you think you need to get surgery?
아닐걸. 괜찮을걸. 우리가 출발 전에 약을 먹었으니
When you get to the summit of this mountain, the altitude is so high that you might get a headache
143.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

144.meaning: ~지 뭐 expresses resignation or acceptance that the outcome cannot be changed, roughly I guess so or then I will.
144.when_to_use: Use it when the speaker stops worrying about the result and accepts a practical next step.
144.how_to_build: Attach ~지 뭐 to the relevant conjugated predicate; the tone and context carry the resigned attitude described by HTSK.
examples: 매운 떡볶이를 먹으면 입안이 얼얼해서 그냥 순한 맛 떡볶이를 시키지 뭐
When I eat spicy ttokboki the inside of my mouth gets all tingly, so I guess we just need to order the plain
부가세를 깜박해서 생각보다 가격이 비싸서 이 컴퓨터 말고 다른 컴퓨터를 사지 뭐
I forgot about the tax, so the price is more expensive than I thought, which means I guess I won’t be able to buy this computer, and I’ll have to buy another one instead
샤워를 하고 머리를 안 말려서 지금 머리가 곱슬머리인데 나가야 되면 모자를 쓰지 뭐
After showering I didn’t dry my hair and now my hair is all curly, so if I have to go outside I guess I’ll just wear a hat
관련 통계에 대한 수치를 보면 그 문제에 대한 답을 찾을 수 있겠지 뭐
If we look at the relevant statistic figures, I guess we can just find and answer
144.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

145.meaning: ~란 is a shortened quotation or definition form related to ~(이)란 말이다 and related expressions.
145.when_to_use: Use it when defining, labeling or emphasizing what a word or concept is, especially in conversational explanations.
145.how_to_build: Use noun + 이란/란 according to the consonant-vowel rule and follow the contracted quotation patterns in the official lesson.
examples: 오늘 비가 올 거라 우산을 가져가란 일기예보를 까먹었어요
It will rain today, and I forgot about the rain forecast telling us to bring an umbrella
그 여자가 임신한 아이가 남자아이란 것은 제 추측이에요
It is my guess that the baby that woman is pregnant with is a boy
저의 가장 친한친구가 쌍둥이란 것을 지금까지 몰랐어요
Until now, I didn’t know that my best friend is (has) a twin
땀띠가 있어서 이 연고를 바르란 아빠의 말을 무시했어요
I have a heat rash, and I didn’t listen (ignored) the words/advice from my dad to put ointment on it
145.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

146.meaning: ~느라고 gives a reason based on being occupied with one action, usually with a negative or inconvenient result.
146.when_to_use: Use it when one activity prevents, delays or causes difficulty for another action.
146.how_to_build: Attach ~느라고 to a verb stem; the subject and tense restrictions and the negative-result nuance are important in HTSK.
examples: 주가가 떨어져서 많은 사람들이 고통 받고 있어요
The stock prices are falling so a lot of people are suffering
제가 육상을 좋아해서 육상대회에 매번 참가했어요
I like track-and-field so I attended the track events every time
제가 새를 싫어해서 우리 가족은 앵무새를 키우지 않았어요
I don’t like birds so my family never had a pet parrot (never raised a parrot)
제가 시금치를 안 사서 대신에 철분이 시금치 만큼 많이 있는 소고기를 샀어요
I didn’t buy spinach so instead I bought beef, which has as much iron content as spinach
146.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

147.source_title: Because of an unexpected event with ~는 바람에
147.meaning: ~는 바람에 means because of an unexpected or uncontrollable event, often with a negative result.
147.when_to_use: Use it to explain an undesirable consequence caused by a sudden situation.
147.how_to_build: Use the present modifier ~는 before 바람에 and add the cause clause; the main clause states the unexpected result.
examples: 속옷 바람으로
in one’s underwear
잠옷 바람으로
in one’s pajamas
내복 바람으로
in one’s long underwear
속옷 바람으로 밖에서 빨래를 널었어요
I hung the laundry outside in my underwear
147.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

148.meaning: ~고는 하다 and the contracted ~곤 하다 describe a habitual or repeated action, often in the past.
148.when_to_use: Use them for things someone regularly used to do or would often do.
148.how_to_build: Attach ~고는 하다 to the verb and contract it to ~곤 하다 in speech; conjugate 하다 for tense and politeness.
examples: 저는 종종 스트레스가 쌓일 때 마다 잡지책을 사곤 해요
When stressed piles up every now and then I buy a magazine
원만히 연애를 하고 결혼하는 커플이 더 행복하게 살곤 해요
Couples who have an amicable relationship and get married often live happily
사람들은 섣부르게 주식에 투자를 시작했다가 망하곤 해요
People often start investing in stocks too hastily and get ruined
이 늪은 다른 늪보다 훨씬 깊어서 일년에 한 명 이상씩 이 늪에 빠져 죽곤 해요
This swamp is much deeper than others, so every year there is more than one person that falls into it and drowns
148.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

149.source_title: Unfortunately / of all things with 하필
149.meaning: 하필 means unfortunately, of all things or at the worst possible choice/time.
149.when_to_use: Use it to highlight an especially unlucky, unexpected or inconvenient selection.
149.how_to_build: Place 하필 before the word or clause being singled out; it is an adverb and does not take a productive ending.
examples: 하필 밥을 다 차리고 먹기 전에 전화가 와서 통화하는 바람에 밥이 다 식었어
I got all of the food ready and right before I was about to eat, of all things, the phone rang and because I was talking on the phone, the food got all cold
된장국을 끓이려고 감자를 샀는데 하필 뜨거운 전자레인지 위에 올려놓아서 감자가 다 썩었어
I bought potatoes so I could boil up some bean-paste soup, but of all places, I put the potatoes on top of the microwave and they got hot and rotted
얼렁뚱땅 거짓말을 하고 넘어가려고 했는데 하필 같이 있던 친구가 사실을 말하는 바람에 난감해졌어
I told a lie and wanted to just go past it but, of all people, one of my friends who was there told everybody the truth so I got really embarrassed
좋은 자리에서 공연을 보려고 사람들을 비집고 자리를 잡았는데 하필 내가 싫어하는 사람 옆에 서서 공연을 보게 됐어
In order to get a good spot to see the performance I pushed my way through the people and got a spot, but of all people I ended up having to watch the performance next to somebody I don’t like
149.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

150.meaning: 어쩐지 means no wonder, as expected or somehow, connecting a new realization with a reason or intuition.
150.when_to_use: Use it when a result now makes sense or when the speaker had a vague feeling about it.
150.how_to_build: Place 어쩐지 before the clause and conjugate the rest normally; learn the discourse use from HTSK examples.
examples: 어쩐지 그 아이가 음식만 보면 바로 집어삼켰어요
No wonder that baby devoured his food at the very sight of it
어쩐지 그 아이가 음식만 보면 바로 집어삼켜서 무슨 성격상 문제가 있는 줄 알았어요
No wonder that baby devoured his food at the very sight of it, I thought there was something wrong with his personality
어쩐지 그 사람이 야구를 하는 게 어색해 보였어요
No wonder that person looks strange playing baseball
어쩐지 그 사람이 왼손잡이를 위해 만들어진 글러브를 끼고 야구를 하는 게 어색해 보였어요
That person wore gloves made for a left-handed person, so no wonder he looked so strange playing baseball
150.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

151.meaning: Korean onomatopoeia imitates sounds, including the vivid sound words introduced in this lesson.
151.when_to_use: Use sound-symbolic words to make descriptions, narratives and actions more vivid and expressive.
151.how_to_build: Learn each sound word with the action or sound it describes; reduplication and final particles follow the examples on the official page.
examples: 문고리를 잡고 계속해서 움직였더니 덜커덕 소리가 나고 문이 열렸다
I held the doorknob and kept moving it and then a ‘clank’ sound came out and the door opened
윗집은 밤만 되면 아이들이 우당탕 뛰어다녀서 매우 시끄럽다
When it’s nighttime, the kids of the floor above us run around and ‘slam’ the floor so it is really loud
도둑을 잡은 경찰은 바로 수갑을 철커덩 채우고 경찰서로 도둑을 데려갔다
The police that caught the thief put him in handcuffs right away and brought him to the police station
바람이 세게 불자 갑자기 문이 바람에 철컥 닫혔다
It was very windy, so the door ‘clanked’ closed in the wind
151.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

152.meaning: Korean mimetic words describe manner, movement, appearance or a state rather than a literal sound.
152.when_to_use: Use them to add vivid detail about how an action happens or what a scene looks and feels like.
152.how_to_build: Treat each mimetic expression as vocabulary; use the repeated or modified form and the particles shown by HTSK.
examples: 술을 바닥에 쏟아서 바닥이 끈적거려요
I spilled alcohol all over the floor and now the floor is sticky
걸레로 바닥을 열심히 닦아서 바닥이 반들거려요
I wiped the floor really hard with a rag and now the floor is all shiny
목이 너무 말라서 물을 꿀꺽거리면서 급하게 마셨어요
I was so thirsty that I urgently gulped down water
많은 학생들이 잠에 취해 꾸벅거리면서 수업을 들었어요
A lot of students dose off in class because they’re so tired
152.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

153.meaning: ~려 expresses an intention or purpose, often a shortened or literary form related to trying or intending to do something.
153.when_to_use: Use it when describing an aim or an action someone is about to attempt.
153.how_to_build: Attach ~려 to a verb stem and complete the construction with the following verb or noun phrase described in HTSK.
examples: 출판물을 준비하려니까 자료를 많이 모아야 해요
I tried to prepare the publication, so I had to gather a lot of materials
새 출판사를 찾으려니까 여러 출판물을 읽어 봤어요
I tried to find a new publisher, so I read various publications
경쟁자보다 앞서려니까 더 열심히 노력해야 했어요
I tried to get ahead of my competitor, so I had to work harder
밖에서 들어오는 찬바람을 막으려니까 테이프가 필요했어요
I tried to block the cold wind blowing from the outside, so I needed tape
153.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

154.meaning: ~려다가 connects an intention or action that was about to happen with a different result or interruption.
154.when_to_use: Use it when someone intended to do one thing but changed course or was stopped.
154.how_to_build: Attach ~려다가 to the verb stem and put the changed action or outcome in the following clause.
examples: 한가지만 사려다가 여러 가지를 샀어요
I was going to buy just one thing, but I ended up buying several things
우리는 주말에 가족과 함께 초원에서 피크닉을 즐겼어요
We enjoyed a picnic with the family in the meadow over the weekend
초원에 가려다가 날씨가 안 좋아서 포기했어요
I was going to go to the meadow, but I gave up because of the bad weather
대도시의 복잡한 생활은 저를 가끔 지치게 해요
The hectic life in the big city sometimes makes me tired
154.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

155.meaning: ~려는 and ~려던 describe an intention or an action that someone was trying or planning to do.
155.when_to_use: Use ~려는 for an active current intention and ~려던 for a past or interrupted intention.
155.how_to_build: Attach the present or past modifier after ~려 before the noun, usually 것, 사람 or 참, following the source forms.
examples: 압정을 사용하려는 사람들이 많아서 압정이 금방 다 팔렸어요
Many people wanted to use thumbtacks, so they quickly sold out
한국어를 배우는 학생이 별로 없어요
There aren’t a lot of students who are learning Korean
한국어를 배우려고 하는 학생이 별로 없어요
There aren’t a lot of students who are trying to learn Korean
한국어를 배우려는 학생이 별로 없어요
There aren’t a lot of students who are trying to learn Korean
155.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

156.meaning: Further uses of ~(으)려 include the expression ~려는 참이다, being just about to do something, and related intention forms.
156.when_to_use: Use it to say that an action is imminent or that someone is in the middle of preparing to do it.
156.how_to_build: Attach ~려 or ~(으)려 to the verb stem and combine it with 참 or the following construction shown in HTSK.
examples: 여름날에 해변에 가려던 참인데 갑자기 비가 왔어요
I was about to go to the beach on a summer day, but it suddenly started raining

159.how_to_build: Use the contracted form attached to the relevant verb or adjective as shown in HTSK; do not treat 치 as a general negative suffix for every word.

160.meaning: ~느냐 is a plain or formal question form used inside complex questions and quoted constructions.
160.when_to_use: Use it when embedding or presenting a question about an action, state or reason in advanced Korean.
160.how_to_build: Attach the appropriate form of 느냐 to the predicate and combine it with particles or quotation endings according to the source patterns.
examples: 물기가 아직 남아 있느냐 없느냐가 문제예요
The issue is whether there are still droplets left or not

161.meaning: ~느냐는 turns a question clause into a noun-modifying expression: the question of whether or what someone does.
161.when_to_use: Use it before nouns such as question, discussion, rumor or judgment when the content of the question is being described.
161.how_to_build: Attach ~느냐는 to the question clause, then add the noun it modifies; follow the verb, adjective and tense forms shown by HTSK.
examples: 우리가 이번 프로젝트를 제시간에 끝낼 수 있느냐는 질문이 제기되었어요

162.meaning: ~느냐에 따라서 means depending on whether or how a situation is, with the result varying accordingly.
162.when_to_use: Use it when a result changes according to an answer, choice or condition expressed as a question clause.
162.how_to_build: Attach ~느냐에 따라(서) to the question clause, then state the result or difference in the main clause.
examples: 예선에서 얼마나 잘 하느냐에 따라서 본선에 진출할 수 있을지가 결정돼요
Whether you advance to the finals depends on how well you do in the preliminaries
동물이 얼마나 심한 학대를 받았느냐에 따라서 회복 시간이 달라져요
The recovery time depends on how severe the animal’s abuse was

163.meaning: 말이지 is a conversational ending used to explain, emphasize or remind, roughly you know or I mean.
163.when_to_use: Use it when clarifying an attitude or drawing attention to the point just made in informal speech.
163.how_to_build: Attach 말이지 to the relevant predicate or noun phrase; use the conversational form and intonation described in HTSK.

164.meaning: ~단 말이지 emphasizes or insists on a statement, with a tone such as you see, I mean or I am saying that.
164.when_to_use: Use it to stress a claim or make the listener recognize the point, especially in conversation.
164.how_to_build: Build it from the quoted form + 다는 말이지 and use the contraction ~단 말이지 as shown by HTSK.
examples: 범인이 계속 도망 다니고 있는데 경찰이 빨리 체포하다 못 하면 더 큰 사고가 날 수도 있어. 하루빨리 수사를 제대로 해야 말이지.

165.meaning: ~(으)니 말이지 adds a reason or relief-like explanation with the feeling that this is why or fortunately.

165.how_to_build: Attach ~니 말이지 after a vowel or ㄹ and ~으니 말이지 after another consonant, then complete the conversational sentence.

166.meaning: ~(이)야말로 means precisely, truly or this is the one that especially fits the description.

167.meaning: ~ㄹ/을까 말까 means whether to do something or not and expresses indecision.

178.meaning: ~구요 is a spoken connective ending that adds another related fact or explanation, often with a soft conversational tone.

At first, his explanation sounded plausible, and everyone was fooled

The children warmly greeted their grandmother holding her hand tightly, and she shed tears

Large projects are bound to go through many difficulties before succeeding

The old theater sign still seems to be flashing electric lights

The teacher maintained a calm expression throughout the presentation

He criticized the remake without even having appreciating the original work

182.meaning: ~답다 means characteristic of, worthy of or like the qualities associated with a noun.

Even from a third party’s perspective, that wasn’t something a real friend would do

184.meaning: ~(이)나마 means at least or even if it is only that much, often acknowledging an imperfect option.

That problem is not only international but also difficult to solve

197.meaning: 바 is a formal noun-like expression used in legal, official and written language for a fact, point, manner or previously stated matter.
197.when_to_use: Use it in formal announcements, contracts and statements such as as stated or in view of the fact that.
197.how_to_build: Use the modifier before 바, including V-ㄴ/은 바 or the fixed constructions in HTSK; add particles such as 에, 와 or 로 as required.

201.meaning: ~(으)리, commonly in ~(으)리라고, expresses a formal or literary prediction, intention or belief about what will happen.
201.when_to_use: Use it in formal writing, speeches and reported expectations, especially with 생각하다 or 믿다.

202.meaning: ~(으)려니 expresses an assumption or expectation that the speaker accepts, often with a resigned or matter-of-fact tone.
